name: SHA Wellness Clinic
who: Oceanfront medical-wellness flagship, 4-21 night stays, macrobiotic cuisine and full diagnostic medicine; from ~$900/night.
why: The clinic most other medical resorts get compared to; pioneered the integrative-medicine-plus-fitness format in Europe.
takeaway: Come for the diagnostics and leave with a protocol — this is medicine with a resort attached.

name: SHA Mexico
who: SHA's Caribbean sister clinic on a private beach, same integrative-medicine method as the Spain original; from ~$900/night.
why: Brings the SHA method to the Americas with a beachfront setting the Spain original lacks.
takeaway: Come for the same SHA integrative-medicine method as Spain, now with a Caribbean beach attached.

name: Lanserhof Tegernsee
who: Modernist medical health resort built around the Lanserhof/F.X. Mayr cure, with in-house physicians and diagnostics; from ~$1,100/night.
why: Widely cited as the benchmark European medical spa; the architecture and Mayr-cure protocol both get copied.
reach: IG ~112K brand-wide @lanserhof (verified 2026-08, no site-specific handle found)
takeaway: Come for the Mayr-cure medical protocol under physician supervision, not a leisure spa break.

name: Lanserhof Sylt
who: Lanserhof's newer North Sea-island outpost, dune-set architecture and the same medical Mayr-cure program; from ~$1,100/night.
why: Extends the Lanserhof standard to Germany's most exclusive island resort market.
reach: IG ~112K brand-wide @lanserhof (verified 2026-08, no site-specific handle found)
takeaway: Come for the same medical Mayr-cure protocol as Lanserhof's flagship, in a dune-set island setting — not a beach vacation.

name: Chenot Palace Weggis
who: Lake Lucerne palace hotel running the Chenot Method detox and diagnostics program in a 5,000 sqm medical spa; from ~$1,000/night.
why: Henri Chenot's original detox methodology, now franchised worldwide, still headquarters here.
takeaway: Come for the original Chenot Method detox and diagnostics program, not just a lakeside palace stay.

name: Clinique La Prairie
who: Lake Geneva longevity clinic operating since 1931, revitalization and cellular-therapy programs plus a full fitness and movement wing; from ~$1,500/night.
why: The longest-running name in medical longevity tourism; near-century of celebrity clientele and press.
takeaway: Book this for clinical longevity treatments and cellular therapy, with fitness support alongside — not a standard spa weekend.

name: Palazzo Fiuggi
who: Early-1900s palace near Rome converted in 2021 into a high-tech longevity clinic with full diagnostics, gym, and Pilates/yoga studios; from ~$1,300/night.
why: Fastest-rising name in medical wellness; Oprah's publicly named favorite and a 2025 Condé Nast Best Destination Spa winner.
takeaway: Book it for high-tech longevity diagnostics with movement studios attached — a clinic stay, not a palace vacation.

name: Sensei Lanai, A Four Seasons Resort
who: Larry Ellison and Dr. David Agus's evidence-based wellbeing retreat on a private Hawaiian island, with app-guided programming and full diagnostics; from ~$2,000/night.
why: Backed by one of the world's richest men and a leading oncologist; the reference case for data-driven, science-led wellness.
takeaway: Come for a personally guided science program on a private island — this suits data-driven wellness travelers, not beach loungers.

name: Sensei Porcupine Creek
who: Sensei's desert retreat on Larry Ellison's former estate, 22 rooms, golf, tennis and evidence-based wellness programming; from ~$2,000/night.
why: Confirmed open and operating in 2026; expands the Sensei method into the Palm Springs desert wellness market.
takeaway: Book this for the Sensei evidence-based wellness program on a small, private desert estate — not a golf getaway.

name: Preidlhof
who: Adults-only alpine dolce-vita resort with a large spa, gym and movement studios above the fitness-hotel tier but below clinical-medical; from ~$600/night.
why: One of South Tyrol's best-known luxury wellness names, though closer to a premium spa hotel than a medical clinic.
takeaway: Book this for movement studios and spa in the Alps — premium spa comfort, not a medical program.

name: Grand Resort Bad Ragaz
who: 150-year-old thermal-water resort with an onsite medical clinic and rehab center alongside spa and golf; from ~$700/night.
why: One of Europe's oldest medical-thermal resorts, still ranked among the continent's top medical wellness properties.
takeaway: Come for medical clinic and rehab care alongside thermal water and golf — clinical, not purely a spa trip.

name: Villa Stephanie at Brenners Park-Hotel & Spa
who: The medical-spa wing of the historic Brenners Park hotel, offering health checks and body programs alongside a grand-hotel stay; from ~$700/night.
why: A storied European spa-town address, though its Instagram presence and program now run under the main Brenners Park account.
warning: Villa Stephanie's own Instagram account has been folded into the main Brenners Park-Hotel handle.
takeaway: Book this for health checks and body programs within a grand historic hotel — medical wing, not standalone clinic.

name: VIVAMAYR Maria Wörth
who: Lakeside medical health resort built on F.X. Mayr digestive medicine, with full diagnostics, movement and nutrition coaching; from ~$700/night.
why: One of the two flagship VIVAMAYR sites that popularized the Mayr cure internationally.
takeaway: Come for the Mayr-cure digestive protocol with full diagnostics — medical resort, not a lakeside holiday.

name: VIVAMAYR Altaussee
who: VIVAMAYR's smaller alpine-lake outpost, same Mayr-cure medical program in a quieter mountain setting; from ~$650/night.
why: Extends the VIVAMAYR medical method to a second, more secluded Austrian lake location.
reach: IG follower count not separately confirmed; brand-wide @vivamayr and @vivamayrmariawoerth verified 2026-08
takeaway: Come for the same Mayr-cure protocol as VIVAMAYR's flagship, in a quieter, more secluded alpine setting.

name: Buchinger Wilhelmi
who: The original medically supervised therapeutic-fasting clinic, running since the 1920s, with daily movement and physician oversight; from ~$500/night.
why: The clinic that invented modern medical fasting; still the most cited name in fasting research and longevity press.
takeaway: Book a medically supervised fasting stay with physician oversight — this is the original fasting clinic, not a diet retreat.

name: RAKxa Integrative Wellness
who: Riverside medical-wellness retreat blending Western diagnostics with Ayurveda, Traditional Chinese and Thai medicine, plus fitness and movement studios; from ~$600/night.
why: Thailand's leading medical-integrative resort, from the founders of Chiva-Som, and a fast-growing regional benchmark.
takeaway: Book this for blended Western diagnostics and Ayurvedic/TCM medicine with structured movement — medical-integrative, not a spa trip.

name: Zulal Wellness Resort by Chiva-Som
who: The Middle East's largest immersive medical wellness resort, gender-segregated wings, full diagnostics and structured movement programs; from ~$800/night.
why: Qatar's flagship wellness investment and the region's biggest medical-resort infrastructure play.
takeaway: Book this for full medical diagnostics and structured movement in gender-segregated wings — a medical resort, not a spa hotel.

name: Joali Being
who: A private Maldivian island fully dedicated to well-living rather than à la carte spa, with personalised Mind/Skin/Microbiome/Energy programmes and daily movement; from ~$2,000/night.
why: The first Maldives resort built entirely around structured wellbeing science rather than beach-and-spa leisure.
takeaway: Book a personalized wellbeing-science programme here — structured, not a beach-and-spa island holiday.

name: Longevity Health & Wellness Hotel
who: Coastal Algarve hotel focused on longevity health checks, detox and fitness programming at a more accessible price point; from ~$350/night.
why: A smaller-scale entry point into medical-longevity tourism, more affordable than the Alpine and Swiss clinics.
takeaway: Book this for longevity health checks and detox at an accessible price — a budget entry to medical wellness.
